name: inline
title: Launcher action, in line: a pusher between two curved arms shaped by the beam solver, a flooded frame, the disc flat in a roofed slot, the pull ring on top, a solid trigger that is its own sear on a hinge carrying the pull, printed in one piece on its side
orientation: On its side, as drawn: one piece, no supports. Put a finger through the ring and pull it back until it clicks: the pusher slides straight back between the arms, and the tooth under the stem rides over the trigger's hook and catches. Let go of the ring, then pull the trigger back with a finger in the crook in front of it: the hook slides off the tooth and the pusher throws the disc.

body.label: The action: frame, arms and pusher in one print

height_min.rule: The least it may print, on its side: tall enough that the frame and the pusher don't bend out of their plane

height_max.rule: The most it may print: the shaping prints it as tall as it must be, between these, to store the energy (an arm's force goes as its height; its strain doesn't)

gap.rule: The least gap between parts printed in place that still prints apart

slide.rule: The disc's gap each side in its barrel: what slid best on the fit test plate

fit.rule: The pusher's room in its pocket and barrel, each side: the fit test's sliding gap and a little more, so it doesn't drag

room.rule: The arms' room each side, round wherever they go: more than the print gap, so they don't drag on the frame

spring_clear.rule: The springs' room each side: more than the print gap, so the frame is clear of them however they ring as the shot goes

stroke.rule: How far the ring pulls the shuttle back to draw it: the launcher's travel, longer than 0.8's 12 now the arms' room runs further back

short.rule: The ring is drawn this much short of the stroke the arms were shaped for: the frame stops the pusher a sliding gap past the draw, within the arms' finite-element limit

energy.rule: What the spring stores drawn: the launcher's stored energy

safety.rule: The arms' strain limit is PETG's strength over its modulus (its yield strain) over this

margin.rule: The arms are shaped to this share of the strain limit, so the finite-element peak (rounds and all) has room

least.rule: The thinnest an arm may get: three lines (two-line flexures flexed and twisted in the flat action's print)

most.rule: The thickest an arm may get

arm_gap.rule: How far apart an arm's own loops keep: more than the print gap, so they print apart and don't slap together when it fires

arm_bend.rule: The tightest an arm may curve, in its thicknesses: tighter, its inside takes much more strain than beam theory says

legs.rule: The arms start from a meander of this many legs folded into their room (odd), and the shaping moves every point and thickness from there

bend_lo.rule: Where the starting meander's low bends turn, above the axis

evaluations.rule: How many shapes the shaping may try

bar.rule: The pusher bar's height: solid, so it doesn't bend (the flat action's windowed bar did)

bar_back.rule: The shuttle's block, where the arms meet it, runs this far either side of their tips: no further, since every gram it carries is a gram the disc doesn't get

nose_w.rule: The nose's width in the plane: the hollow the disc's edge sits in

rise.rule: The arms' room, from the bar's top to the frame's inside

reach.rule: How far behind where they meet the shuttle's block the arms' room reaches: back to just ahead of the ring's room, which the trigger no longer shares

room_front.rule: The arms' room ends here, a little ahead of where they meet the block: ahead of it, under the shuttle, is the catch's

root_x.rule: Where each arm grows from the frame, behind where it meets the block: so the arms pull on the closed back of the frame, not on its front

wall.rule: The frame round the arms' room, and the blocks they grow from

least_frame.rule: The thinnest the flooded frame may be anywhere: thinner bits are left out

band.rule: The frame is solid this far round everything that moves and the outline's edge: everywhere, no windows, so it doesn't bend on to the disc or the shuttle under the springs' pull

stem_h.rule: The slide's stem's height in the plane: stout, with room for the pocket the shuttle's tail head runs in and a wall either side

ring_x.rule: The pull ring's centre: on top of the slide's stem, behind the arms' room

guide_depth.rule: The ridge on the stem's sides that runs in a groove in the handle, at the middle of the print's height, flanks at 45°

bridge_foot.rule: How far the roof (and a guide's strip) stands on the frame either side of what it spans

bridge_gap.rule: The gap between the disc and the roof over its slot, in layers

roof_span.rule: The widest the roof over the disc's slot may bridge: the X1C bridges this far, by the user's judgement (the rule's 5 mm is cautious), to be proved on the print

ring_in.rule: The pull ring's hole: a finger through it

handle.rule: Solid behind the drawn ring and stem: the handle

into.rule: How far an arm runs on into the wall and the bar, so they join solidly

spring_round.rule: The round where each arm meets the wall and the bar

tooth.rule: The catch's tooth: how far it hangs below the spine

tooth_w.rule: The tooth's length along the barrel at its foot, half of it flat and half its back's slope

lip_round.rule: The round where the slide's lip meets its bar, inside the recess: no notch for it to snap at

tail_slot.rule: A slot up the middle of the stem's tail, open at its end: the frame's tongue in it guides the stem far behind the front posts, so it can't pitch and wedge

catch_piece.rule: 1 prints the catch test piece: the front half alone (the arms, the shuttle, the catch, the trigger and the tunnel), drawn by a knob on the shuttle's tail; no slide, ring or their spring

piece_back.rule: The test piece's frame runs this far behind the arms' reach and the wall

knob.rule: The test piece's knob: the tail's head drawn out this much further back, as tall as the head, so the frame over it props the tail as the slide's bar does in the whole

knob_hole.rule: A hole down through the knob for a pin or a straightened paperclip, to draw the shuttle back by

spine_top_clear.rule: More room over the spine than the gap: the frame above it bends towards it under the springs' pull

tail_slot_y.rule: The slot's underside: the stem's middle, so the half under it is the stem's whole lower half

tail_tall.rule: Behind the ring the stem's tail stands this high, so the half over the slot is stout there too

tail_slot_len.rule: How far the slot runs up the stem: the slide's whole travel and a good length of tongue in it at rest, ending under the ring's solid back, where the pull goes through

hook_lean.rule: The tail's head leans forward up its front, and the slide's lip with it: drawing, the lip is pulled down on to the head, not lifted off it

tooth_gusset.rule: How much further back the tooth's back slope meets the spine: a filled triangle, wide where it joins the spine, with no neck to bend at

engage.rule: How deep the hook's face reaches up the tooth's: well over the print gap, so the tooth bears on the face, not on its corner

settle.rule: Let go of, the shuttle comes forward this much from the draw on to the hook: more than the hooked face leans back over its depth, so the hook is up before the tooth meets it

sear_reach.rule: The hinge's middle is this far behind where the tooth bears: far enough that the tooth, drawn back, stays clear of the hinge's seat on the trigger

sear_drop.rule: and this far below it, so the hinge's tip and the trigger's shoulder sit low enough for a lip of frame under the shuttle's spine, right behind the tooth, to take the catch's push down

hinge.rule: The trigger's hinge: a flexure on the line from its middle to the tooth, carrying the pull in tension; the trigger turns it about its middle

hinge_round.rule: The round where the hinge meets the frame and the sear

hinge_least.rule: The thinnest the hinge may be: three lines; it carries the pull in tension, which a strip carries easily, and thinner it's lighter to turn

hinge_swing.rule: How far from the pull's line the shaping may turn the hinge's ends

hinge_room.rule: How far below the hinge's middle the shaping may take it

hinge_energy.rule: What the hinge stores with the trigger pulled: enough to bring the sear back up behind the tooth smartly

hold_design.rule: The pull the hinge is shaped to carry: five times this spring's, for the stronger springs to come

hold_give.rule: The most the hinge may give along the pull's line under the design pull: a small fraction of the catch's engagement (under this spring's own pull, about a sixth of it)

hinge_evaluations.rule: How many shapes the hinge's shaping may try

head.rule: The hook's flat top, ahead of its hooked face; its ramp runs on from there down to the trigger's front

chamfer.rule: The hook's and the tooth's meeting corners taken off this much, so they slide past each other as it's drawn

trigger_neck.rule: Its front runs straight down this far from its top, then curves back to its toe

trigger_toe.rule: Its toe, on the frame's bottom: the trigger's front curves down and back to it from under the hook, and the finger sits in that crook

trigger_heel.rule: Its heel, behind: the trigger is solid from the toe to here, leaving the frame between it and the arms wide enough to hold the hinge's root still

heel_h.rule: The heel's height, up from the bottom

trigger_waist.rule: Its back runs up from the heel to this far behind the hinge's tip, under the hinge

hinge_clear.rule: The trigger's back keeps this far below the hinge's line: its thickness, its round and room

trigger_round.rule: Every outside corner of the trigger rounded to this: nothing for a finger to catch on

crook.rule: How deep the hollow the finger sits in is, bowed back from a straight line

crook_steps.rule: Steps the hollow is drawn in

trigger_room.rule: The trigger's room in the frame, all round: a hinge doesn't turn quite about one point, so a little more than the print gap; the frame behind it is its stop

finger_wall.rule: The frame left in front of the finger's room: room for the front corner's plate hole

finger_round.rule: The finger's room's corners rounded to this

finger_at.rule: Where on the crook's face, up from the toe, the finger pulls

pull.rule: How far the trigger turns pulled right back, where the frame behind it stops it: far enough that the hook, camming the shuttle back as its leaning face drops, falls clear of the tooth

friction.rule: Friction between printed PETG faces in the simulation: the trigger pulls against it

plate_pin.rule: The snap pins' diameter (objects/pin) that would hold a plate either side: the frame needn't have them

plate_hole.rule: The holes for them through the frame's corners: the pin and the fit test's pin gap round it

plate_in.rule: How far each hole's centre is in from the frame's edges

plate_wall.rule: Solid frame round each hole, however the web falls

round.rule: Every inside corner of the frame and the pusher rounded to this

spine.rule: The shuttle's spine, from the block forward to the nose, in the plane: thin, since it only carries the tooth's pull and the disc's push

catch_x.rule: The cocked tooth's front, where it bears on the hook: far enough ahead of the arms that the trigger's hinge roots on frame between them

bite.rule: The hooked face leans back past square to the hinge's line by this: the pull turns the trigger up into the tooth, so the catch holds by its shape (the check wants 5°; the rest is for the print)

overshoot.rule: How far the shuttle may run on past rest after the shot, its arms bringing it back: the room left ahead of the tooth and the head, so nothing stops it but the arms

neck_h.rule: The neck's height in the plane

floor_depth.rule: The floor under the disc's way and the shuttle's nose: six layers, so a loose disc can't fall through

floor_gap.rule: The gap over the floor, under what slides on it

ramp.rule: The ramp in front of the hook's flat top, down to the trigger's front, which the tooth rides as it's drawn back

tail_head.rule: The head at the end of the shuttle's tail, this long, which the slide's pocket catches

nose_l.rule: The shuttle's nose, along the barrel: a block as wide as nose_w, its front a hollow the disc's edge sits in

shot_least.rule: The least share of what the arms store the disc must leave with: the arms' own moving mass (about 1.7 g, a third of their 7 g) and the shuttle's cap it near a sixth for a 0.79 g disc, so 0.12 is what this layout can be held to; 0.8.1's heavy pusher gave it 4%

slide_anchor_x.rule: Where the slide's spring meets the stem's underside, at the front of its room: the root far behind it, so the arm is long

slide_root_x.rule: Where the slide's spring grows from the frame's floor, at the back of the handle

slide_lo.rule: The slide's spring's room runs from here, back under the handle behind the stem's drawn end

slide_hi.rule: to here, leaving a column of frame under the stem ahead of it, behind the arms' room, that the stem rests on

slide_energy.rule: What the slide's spring should store drawn: as little as brings the slide home (the thinnest arm the rules allow stores more)

slide_legs.rule: The slide's spring starts from a meander of this many legs

slide_bend.rule: How far in from its room's ends the slide's spring's starting bends turn

slide_evaluations.rule: How many shapes the slide's spring's shaping may try: a long arm in a short room, a hard job

lip.rule: The slide's lip, along the barrel, ahead of the tail's head: it pulls the head back, so it is as stout as the head

plate_low.rule: The fourth plate hole, behind the stem's drawn end: this high, clear of the slide's spring below

plate_low_in.rule: The fourth plate hole's centre in from the frame's back: clear of the slide drawn right back

hinge_travel.rule: How far the hinge is shaped to turn within the strain limit: past the pull, and past where the frame stops it, since turning about one point stretches it too and the limit comes sooner

cam.rule: Room behind the cocked shuttle for the hook's lean to cam it back as the trigger lets it go: more than the engagement over the bite's tangent

face_r.rule: The tooth's face is a little round where it bears, this radius: tipped a little under the load, it rolls on the hook's flat face, so the face's lean still sets the bite

tie_from.rule: A bridge over the shuttle's spine ties the frame under it, where the trigger's hinge roots, to the frame over it, from here

tie_to.rule: to here (the spine passes under it, cut down a little)

spine_guide_from.rule: The spine's top runs in a groove in the frame over it from here

spine_guide_to.rule: to here: the shuttle held across the plane both ways, its nose being between the floor's ledges

stem_guide_from.rule: The slide's stem's top runs in a groove in the frame over it, between the ring and the arms, from here

shuttle_clear.rule: The shuttle's room round it: the print gap, no more, so the catch's pull can't tip it down on to the trigger

load_gap.rule: A loaded disc lies this far ahead of the cocked nose (it rests where it drops in the slot): clear of the nose's creep as the trigger lets go

dip.rule: Room under the cocked tooth over the trigger's top, beyond the gap: the catch's pull, under the springs' line, tips the shuttle's front down a little, and the tooth must not land on the trigger

tie_foot.rule: The tie over the spine stands this far on the frame under it: no further, clear of the hinge below

home_clear.rule: The slide's spring's room each side: the slide sits a little low under the hand's pull on the ring

lower_ledge.rule: The floor's lower ledge starts this far ahead of the slot's back, clear of the trigger's swing

stem_tail.rule: The slide's stem runs on behind the ring this far, into the handle, where it runs in a groove: the slide held across the plane at both ends, so it can't pitch on its guides' play

trigger_floor.rule: The trigger's bottom stands this far up from the frame's edge: the frame's wall under it, whole, with the groove its heel's ridge runs in

slide_slack.rule: The pocket's lips sit this far ahead of the tail's head: room for the shot's run on past rest, and for the slide stopping a little short of home, before the head reaches them

slide_floor.rule: The slide's spring's room stands this far up off the frame's floor: it bulges a little past its room drawn, and the frame's wall under it stays whole

tail_top.rule: The tail's head is a step up off the neck to this height: it sits in a recess open under the stem's front, its lip in front of it, so the slide pitching a little can't wedge it

tail_low.rule: The tail runs low, its underside here: the stem's front over it then has room for a recess the head sits in and a stout bar over that
